items.t: Heineken posts double-digit Q3 growth in Vietnam, CFO warns of tax, margin pressures
Heineken's revenue in Vietnam increased by over 30%.
sum: According to its updated Q3 2026 business report released on October 28th, Heineken stated that Vietnam continues to be one of the company's outstanding growth markets in the Asia-Pacific region.

Specifically, in the third quarter, Heineken's sales volume in Vietnam increased by approximately 20-29%, while net revenue increased by 30-39% compared to the same period last year. This growth was supported by an increase in market share amidst the continued expansion of the beer industry.

The two main brands contributing to business results in Vietnam are Heineken Silver and Tiger Crystal. Heineken Silver continues to maintain its appeal in the premium beer segment, while Tiger Crystal is the driving force behind the growth of the Tiger brand.

Globally, Tiger brand sales increased by 20-29% in the third quarter, primarily driven by the strong performance of Tiger Crystal in Vietnam. Meanwhile, Heineken recorded a 9.7% increase in sales during the quarter, with double-digit growth in 22 markets, including Vietnam.

The results in Vietnam also contributed significantly to Heineken's growth momentum in the Asia-Pacific region. In the third quarter, regional sales volume increased by 17%, while net revenue increased by 15% year-on-year. For the first nine months of the year, these two indicators increased by 13% and 12% respectively.

Heineken stated that Vietnam, China, and India are outstanding growth markets in the region. In India alone, consumption volume increased at a high single-digit rate, while net revenue increased by approximately 20-29%.
For the first nine months of the year, the group's net revenue increased by 4%, while sales volume increased by 3%.

United Breweries stock gains as profit nearly triples in Q2
sum: United Breweries reported a near threefold increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 134.81 crore for the September quarter, helped by volume growth, premiumisation and tighter cost control, The Economic Times reported. Profit rose from Rs 46.34 crore a year earlier, while revenue from operations increased 23.7 percent year over year to Rs 4,623 crore.

EBITDA climbed 108 percent and the margin expanded by 480 basis points, reflecting stronger operating efficiency and cost control. Sell-in volumes rose 16 percent, while premium volumes increased 38 percent, led by Heineken Silver and Kingfisher Ultra.

The strong quarter came with higher expenses, which rose 21.57 percent to Rs 4,481.66 crore. United Breweries expects profitability growth to moderate in the current quarter as raw-material and marketing costs increase, while price increases remain pending across parts of southern India.

The company has said that roughly 30 percent of its business has not yet received price increases. That leaves pricing execution, input costs and the premium portfolio as key variables for margins in the next reporting period.

United Breweries manufactures, markets and sells beer and non-alcoholic beverages in India, with brands including Kingfisher, Heineken Silver and Kingfisher Ultra. The Heineken-controlled brewer is a major participant in India's beer market and competes with international and regional brewers such as AB InBev and Carlsberg India.

Its latest performance shows the benefit of premium products and operating discipline, but the outlook depends on whether pricing actions can offset cost inflation without sacrificing volume or market share.

sum: KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 11): Heineken Malaysia Bhd’s (KL:HEIM) third-quarter net profit fell 38.74% year-on-year, weighed by lower sales volume and operating profit.
Net profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 came in at RM69.18 million compared with RM112.95 million a year earlier, a bourse filing showed.

Revenue for the quarter declined 17.82% to RM539.14 million from RM656.05 million, as sales volume was affected by subdued consumer sentiment, the additional 10% excise duty implemented on Nov 1, 2025, and inventory normalisation among distributors and outlets, which was largely completed in the quarter.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, net profit fell 29.53% to RM224.17 million from RM318.10 million in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue for the nine-month period declined 16.4% to RM1.64 billion from RM1.96 billion.
On its outlook, Heineken Malaysia said the inventory normalisation process was substantially completed, and is expected to conclude in the fourth quarter of this year.

As inventory levels normalise across the trade, the brewer expects demand patterns and business performance to progressively stabilise, although it remains cautious amid prevailing economic and market uncertainties.

sum: Sean Paul headlines the T-Mobile Stage at the T-Mobile Zone at Sphere in Las Vegas on 21 November 2026. The appearance forms part of the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix race weekend.

The Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix runs from 19 to 21 November 2026, with the live music programme centred on the T-Mobile Stage at the T-Mobile Zone at Sphere. The Las Vegas Grand Prix programme places the Jamaican artist on Saturday, 21 November.

The performance takes place beneath Sphere’s Exosphere, within a festival-style race-week setting that combines live music with the wider Grand Prix experience. Natasha Bedingfield is also listed for the Saturday bill, while the event announcement names additional performances by Gorgon City, Ja Rule, Collect 200 and DJ Mandy.

The Jamaican rapper, singer and songwriter has remained a prominent dancehall voice for more than two decades. His catalogue includes the albums Dutty Rock, The Trinity, Imperial Blaze, Tomahawk Technique, Full Frequency, Live N Livin and Scorcha.

The Recording Academy credits him with a Grammy for Best Reggae Album for Dutty Rock. The album’s songs Get Busy and Temperature remain central to the profile described in the Las Vegas programme, which also points to his collaborations with Beyoncé, Sia, Clean Bandit, Dua Lipa and David Guetta. Further career details appear in the Recording Academy biography.

The Las Vegas engagement places Sean Paul’s dancehall sound alongside a broader programme of pop, electronic and hip-hop performances. The T-Mobile Zone at Sphere is part of the Grand Prix’s three-night entertainment schedule, giving the Saturday appearance a setting that is connected to both the concert programme and the race weekend.

Sean Paul’s place on the bill is specific to Saturday, 21 November 2026. The programme identifies him as the Saturday act and presents Natasha Bedingfield alongside him, while the other named performers appear elsewhere across the wider weekend schedule.

Quiñenco stock linked to CCU as S&P keeps outlook negative
sum: On October 29, 2026, S&P Global Ratings affirmed Compania Cervecerias Unidas S.A.'s BBB issuer credit rating and kept its outlook negative. The rating agency cited pressure from changing consumer habits, macroeconomic volatility and limited headroom in CCU's credit metrics.

S&P expects CCU's adjusted leverage to remain above 2.0 times in 2026 before declining below that level in 2027. The agency forecasts revenue growth of 6.3 percent in 2026 and expects the EBITDA margin to recover to 13.2 percent from 12.5 percent in 2025.

The analysis identifies Argentina as a key sensitivity for CCU's international business, while persistent inflation and weaker household purchasing power continue to weigh on discretionary consumption. S&P also views the acquisition of the remaining stake in Aguas CCU-Nestlé Chile as supportive of CCU's strategic control in the water category, although the transaction reduced accessible cash and lifted projected 2026 leverage.

CCU is a multicategory beverage company operating in Chile, Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Paraguay and Uruguay. S&P states that Inversiones y Rentas, a joint venture between Quiñenco and Heineken Chile, directly and indirectly owns 65.87 percent of CCU's shares, with each partner holding 50 percent of the joint venture.

This structure makes CCU's operating performance and credit trajectory relevant to Quiñenco's diversified Chilean business portfolio. The negative outlook is an assessment of CCU's credit profile rather than a direct rating action on Quiñenco.

Quiñenco's investor-relations calendar lists November 27, 2026 for its next earnings release. Investors will be watching whether the group's subsequent disclosures provide further detail on portfolio performance, capital allocation and the contribution of its operating holdings.

items.t: HEINEKEN USA AND OPENTABLE PARTNER TO REWARD AND CELEBRATE DESIGNATED DRIVERS
sum: ''There's No Such Thing As Fine to Drive" program expands, turning reservation booking into a seamless tool for responsible driving.

WHITE PLAINS, N.Y., July 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HEINEKEN USA has announced a first-of-its-kind partnership with OpenTable, enabling diners to designate a driver directly in the booking process. Rooted in HEINEKEN USA's There's No Such Thing As Fine to Drive program, the partnership was sparked by a recent survey finding 71% of Americans would be more likely to make a safe ride home plan if they were prompted at time of reservation booking. The partnership will help remove the barriers to making responsible decisions and celebrate and reward the DD --"The Hero" of the night according to 58% of Americans.

"HEINEKEN has a longstanding global ambition to brew the joy of true togetherness, which means ensuring moments of connection are always enjoyed responsibly and removing barriers to moderation." said Anne de Graaf, Chief Corporate Affairs Officer at HEINEKEN USA. "By elevating the DD experience, we want to raise awareness that opting out of alcohol doesn't mean opting out of the fun. Our pioneering Heineken 0.0 ensures 100% of the social connection and zero judgment. This first-of-its-kind OpenTable partnership proves that choosing not to drink is a celebrated choice, shifting how people plan their nights out from the very first reservation."

"OpenTable is always looking for meaningful ways to connect diners and restaurants," said Reece Jones, General Manager, OpenTable Media. "We're thrilled to partner with HEINEKEN USA through OpenTable's tailored media solutions to do just that, while jointly delivering a new way to bring awareness for responsible consumption into the reservation process."
- The Inclusive Dinner Party: 49% of Americans say that drinking non-alcoholic beer helps them feel included in social moments when they are not consuming alcohol.
- The Key to a Better Experience: 82% of Americans say they can enjoy their day/night of drinking more knowing they have a safe ride home planned in advance.
- The Reservation Blindspot: 57% of Americans say that planning a designated driver/safe ride home is not something they typically think about when making restaurant or venue reservations.

Heineken Malaysia Berhad's (KLSE:HEIM) Conservative Accounting Might Explain Soft Earnings
sum: Investors were disappointed with the weak earnings posted by Heineken Malaysia Berhad (KLSE:HEIM ). Despite the soft profit numbers, our analysis has optimistic about the overall quality of the income statement.
Examining Cashflow Against Heineken Malaysia Berhad's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Heineken Malaysia Berhad has an accrual ratio of -0.18 for the year to March 2026. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of RM544m, well over the RM441.6m it reported in profit. Heineken Malaysia Berhad's free cash flow actually declined over the last year, which is disappointing, like non-biodegradable balloons.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Happily for shareholders, Heineken Malaysia Berhad produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Based on this observation, we consider it possible that Heineken Malaysia Berhad's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! And on top of that, its earnings per share have grown at 7.9% per year over the last three years. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors.

Europe stocks close mixed after investors digested flurry of earnings
sum: The European stock market closed mixed on Wednesday, as regional investors assessed another flurry of corporate earnings.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 was provisionally higher by 0.1% at the end of the trading session, with major bourses in mixed territory. London's FTSE 100 bucked the trend, and rose more than 1% as investors pivoted to mining and energy stocks.
Wednesday has been another busy day for corporate earnings, with TotalEnergies, Ferrari, and Essilor among those that updated investors on their finances.

Reporting on its full-year earnings before the opening bell, Dutch brewer Heineken said it would cut between 5,000 and 6,000 jobs over the next two years. The company, which cited "challenging market conditions," is currently in the midst of a turnaround strategy to accelerate growth by 2030. Total production volumes fell 1.2% over the course of 2025, Heineken said, while operating profit was up 4.4% from the previous year.
The company said it expects operating profit to grow in the range of 2% to 6% this year. Shares of Heineken were about 4% higher by the end of the day.
Meanwhile, shares of French software giant Dassault Systèmes plunged more than 20% after the company's full-year earnings report was published.
Total revenue for the year was flat at a weaker-than-expected 6.24 billion euros ($7.43 billion), and software revenue also showed little growth at 5.64 billion euros.

sum: ZOETERWOUDE – Dolf van den Brink (CEO Heineken) tijdens de opening bij van het Dr. H.P. Heineken Centre in de Heineken brouwerij. Het Global Research & Development Centre is een onderzoekscentrum waar productontwikkeling plaatsvindt van nieuwe en bestaande biermerken. ANP ROBIN VAN LONKHUIJSEN
The chief executive of Dutch brewer Heineken unexpectedly announced his resignation Monday, as the company grapples with lower beer sales and job cuts in a difficult economic environment.

Dolf van den Brink said he would step down on May 31, Heineken said in a statement, after almost six years at the helm “during which he has guided the company through turbulent economic and political times”.
“I believe this is the right moment,” said Van den Brink, 52.
The change of leader comes at a tricky moment for Heineken, the world’s second-largest brewer after AB InBev.
Its most recent quarterly results, published in October, showed a steep decline in the amount of beer sold, with Europe and the United States driving the drop.
Van den Brink acknowledged at the time that the firm was dealing with a “challenging environment, resulting in a mixed performance”.
